The '''Belcantese Independence Movement''' was the anti-occupation movement that organized Belcantese political independence from the [[Vesperan Empire]]. It grew from cultural, educational, labor, religious, and local political networks developed during the occupation.

== Origins ==

The movement's roots lay in the destruction of pre-conquest institutions after the [[Belcanto Campaign]]. Early activity focused on preserving language, song, local histories, and legal memory through the [[Belcantese Cultural Resistance]].

Over time, cultural preservation became political organization. Underground schools, local committees, couriers, archive keepers, and former regional elites helped maintain the idea of Belcantese self-rule.

== Great War Period ==

During the [[Avant Great War]], the movement became more important as Vesperan military strain weakened imperial administration in Belcanto. Resistance networks prepared local authority, communications, and records for a possible post-imperial transition.

== Independence ==

The collapse of local Vesperan power in Belcanto during 1949 allowed the movement to emerge openly before the formal end of the wider war. It helped establish provisional authority in [[Belgrad]] and supported the [[Declaration of Belcantese Independence]].
